# Demonstrations that pass when enabled, and are known to.
#
# example-demos.yml fails when a @Disabled example demonstration PASSES in every run, because
# its @Disabled reason tells a reader to remove @Disabled to see a detection. The entries below
# are the ones that do that today. They are listed here rather than tolerated silently: a job
# whose failures are all expected gets ignored within a month, and a job with no record of what
# it is ignoring is worse.
#
# Adding a line here is the escalation path, and it needs a reason and an issue. Removing one is
# the goal. A line whose demonstration starts firing again is reported as a warning, not a
# failure - some are timing-dependent, so one green week is not proof.
#
# Format: <class-fqn>#<method>   # why
#
# Tracked in #362.
#
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The list is empty. It held five entries between 2026-08-26 and the fix for #362, and none of
# the five turned out to be what the file recorded them as. Kept here so the next person does not
# re-derive it:
#
#   30-false-sharing        Structural, and correctly so: FalseSharingDetector's findings are off
#                           unless -Dasync-test.experimental.false-sharing=true, because its
#                           offsets are estimates the JVM's layout does not follow. The
#                           demonstration is gone and both directions of the gate are pinned by
#                           ordinary @Tests instead.
#   07-livelock             Recorded as timing-dependent; it was three structural faults.
#                           LivelockDetector treats RUNNABLE as progress on purpose, it reads
#                           dumpAllThreads which excludes virtual threads, and the subject does
#                           make progress under contention. The demonstration is gone; the retry
#                           burn is measured directly.
#   112-try-lock-misuse     Genuinely contention-dependent, and now deterministic: a thread
#                           outside the run holds the lock, so tryLock() fails every time.
#   92-virtual-thread-pinning   Not timing at all: synchronized stopped pinning in JDK 24 (JEP
#                           491) and the detector says so. It fires on JDK 21, which is what
#                           example-demos.yml runs; fifty rounds of a 10ms sleep behind one
#                           monitor was what timed the round out before the gate.
#   90-virtual-thread-carrier-exhaustion   Machine-dependent, and now not: the detector fires
#                           when concurrently blocked virtual threads reach availableProcessors(),
#                           so 8 threads fired on a 4-core runner and never on a 16-core
#                           workstation. 64 threads clears any machine this is likely to run on.
